packages.label: סוֹדוֹת הַתּוֹרָה וְהַכֶּבֶשׁ
packages.label_en: Secrets of Torah and the Ramp
packages.reason: The Temple altar ramp (כבש), the furnace/hidden depths of the world (כבשונו של עולם), and the secrets of Torah (סודות התורה) are three expressions of the same essential dimension: the deep, hidden, ascending dimension of Torah knowledge. Climbing the ramp = penetrating the concealed depths of the world = attaining Torah secrets. In the Torah's argument, whoever advanced further in Torah secrets was appointed leader — all three concepts name the same quality of depth-of-attainment that qualifies one for communal leadership.

packages.label: מִקְדָּשׁ וְשֵׂכֶל
packages.reason: The Temple (מקדש) and the intellect/mind of the tzadikim (שכלם) are two names for the same thing — derived directly from the Talmudic statement (Berakhot 33): 'Whoever has da'at, it is as if the Temple was built in his days.' In this Torah, it is their deep intellectual awareness of God ('the whole earth is full of His glory') that makes the tzadikim ashamed to display hypocrisy. The Temple = the mind that sees God everywhere = the sacred cognitive space that refuses pretense.

packages.label: פַּיִס וְיִפַּיְּסוּ
packages.reason: The lottery/lot system (פיס) and the act of the community entreating/appeasing the leader (יפיסו) are two expressions of the same corrective principle: legitimate leadership can only come through communal consent and the leader's own reluctance. 'Lottery' (פיס) IS 'appeasement' (יפיסו) — in this Torah's reading, the Mishnah's word פיס is interpreted as meaning that the people must implore (יפיסו) the leader to accept office. The same root expresses both the institutional mechanism and the personal dynamic of proper, humble leadership.

packages.label: הַמְמֻנֶּה וְיֵצֶר הָרָע
packages.label_en: The Appointed Officer and the Evil Inclination
packages.reason: The 'Appointed Officer' (ממונה) in the Mishnah who supervised the lottery procedure is read in this Torah as a bechina of the Yetzer Hara — both are the same controlling, supervising evil force that manages the competition for honor and exploits each candidate's desire for leadership. The ממונה IS the יצר הרע: the external figure of corrupt institutional authority is the inner voice of self-interest.

packages.label: הַצְבִּיעוּ וְצְבִיעוּת
packages.label_en: The Command to Display and Religious Hypocrisy
packages.reason: The Mishnaic command 'Raise your fingers!' (הצביעו — so others can count and determine the lot) is read in this Torah as a bechina for 'displaying some hypocrisy before the masses' (שיראה איזה צביעות בפני המון עם). The finger-raising IS the performance of false piety — both express the same act: putting on a public religious show to gain popularity. The double-meaning of the root צב״ע (finger / dyeing / hypocrisy) makes them parallel faces of the same fraudulent self-promotion.
